title: Hazel and the Sigil
premise: Sable Vane, a cartographer of unmapped realms, has spent seven years selling small charms in Corvane, a city that outlawed magic, hiding her gift behind careful anonymity. When tonight's date appears verbatim in a century-old book of prophecies, she is pulled into the vanished country of Elowen, where the last survivors of its destruction believe she is the Sigil-bearer foretold to reopen their sealed borders. To escape — and to free them — Sable must map a door out of a country that no longer exists, discovering along the way that her own forgotten childhood was spent there before it fell. In the end she chooses to stay long enough to redraw Elowen's boundaries from memory and love rather than law, opening the door for its people while stepping through herself, no longer hiding who she is.
about_author: Rosalind Eriksen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any modern atlas. She writes fantasy about borders, memory, and the families we build when our old ones are taken.

chapters.title: The Date That Was Written
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In magic-outlawed Corvane, Sable sells charms by day and charts impossible realms by night. A customer leaves behind an antique prophecy book; inside, tonight's date and her own name are inked a century ago. When the prophecy's hour strikes, the city dissolves around her. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen after years of hiding.

chapters.title: A Country With No Edges
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She wakes in Elowen, a nation erased from every map, sustained by stubborn memory and fading sigils. The survivors — a found family of bakers, soldiers, and children born in exile — insist she is their prophesied Sigil-bearer. Sable denies it, but her cartographer's hand begins drawing doors that open. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging taking root.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Searching the ruined archive for the original border-sigil, Sable uncovers records proving she lived in Elowen as a child — her family helped seal the country to save it, at the cost of everyone inside. The seal is collapsing, and the prophecy demands a bearer who will not survive the redrawing. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal colliding with duty.

chapters.title: Drawn From Memory
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. As Elowen frays into nothing, Sable refuses the prophecy's sacrificial terms and instead maps the country from love: every street the survivors remember, drawn together. Their collective memory becomes the new sigil, and the door opens without a death. Sable steps through carrying Elowen's map — and finally her true name. Emotional beat: identity claimed, home redefined.
